pairs.subject: plan-review
pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/DealReview.tsx:2 The approval window is a human gate over a negotiated deal's terms and money actions (the amount, the checks, the payment), the case the golden path explicitly leaves to hitl-approval ('the real thing is obvious: the diff, the message, the amount'), and a grep of windows/approval/** for objection, planner, challenge, slicing and rationale returned no file, so there is no agent-written plan, plan gate, slicing, objection or self-challenge reader for the subject to govern.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/tableDraft.ts:69 The unit put to the owner is a single typed deal or listing, not a task handed to a planning agent, so nothing exists to slice before a plan.
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/review/why.ts:2 The 'Why?' text restates the deal's own facts to explain the gate. No reader scans a plan for decisions it made without saying so.
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/DealReview.tsx:10 The blocking checks are Rust's fixed checks on a money action, not a chartered critic objecting to a plan's premises before implementation.
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/review/why.ts:3 No model writes or critiques anything on this surface, so there is no draft-then-challenge pass to judge.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/review/Parts.tsx:205 There is no plan gate here. By analogy the market figure would conform: it is a field on the existing approval, has no verdict, shows an unavailable state (Parts.tsx:159 'no reference for this item, so the price check was skipped') and carries its percentile, date and cache status.

pairs.registryProposal: informational-fold-in is worded for plan gates, but its four constraints (a field not a step, no verdict, unavailable as a state, the predicate travels with the number) apply just as well to action-approval gates owned by hitl-approval. This context realizes them on a money-approval surface: the market line in review/Parts.tsx says 'A reference, not a verdict', shows a skipped state when there is no reference, and shows the percentile, check date and cache status. Consider adding hitl-approval to the technique's shared_with, or restating its precondition as 'any existing human gate', so that action gates are not judged not-applicable for a rule they follow.
